sources.citation: Kulick, Don & Angela Terrill. 2019. A Grammar and Dictionary of Tayap. (discussion of Laycock's Bungain fieldnotes D7, D26, D27)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Nothing on Bungain stress; reports that Laycock's Bungain notebooks contain a numbered wordlist (e.g. atop’ 'snake', kwulémbe 'mosquito' — forms carry accent marks) and a few elicited sentences, no analysis.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. n.d. [uploaded 2010-09-16]. Bungain Swadesh List. Internet Archive item rosettaproject_but_swadesh-1, file 162 gloss:form rows incl. pronoun/subject-prefix sets; compiler and source not named; CC BY).
sources.note: Bare phonetic word list (aspiration, dental diacritics, nasal vowels marked) with NO stress or pitch marks anywhere (e.g. 'mosquito: kɪlɛmbe' vs Laycock's accent-marked kwulémbe) and no prose; wordlist-only data, not a statement.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In Pawley et al. (eds), Papuan Pasts, PL 572: 109-144.
sources.note: Only Proto-Marienberg pronoun forms; nothing on Bungain phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Sanders, Arden G. & Joy Sanders. 1980. Defining the centres of the Marienberg language family. In Boxwell et al. (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 20, Pacific Linguistics A-56: 171-196. DOI 10.15144/PL-A56.171
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical survey (3 Bungain wordlists), cognate percentages (Bungain 18% avg), sociolinguistic questionnaire, and fn. 5 reassigning Bungain from Laycock's Sepik-Ramu Gapun stock to Torricelli on the basis of subject prefixes; no phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, D.C. & J. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study vol. 1, Pacific Linguistics C-38: 731-763 (sec. 2.11.3.4 Gapun sub-phylum-level family)
sources.note: Nothing on Bungain; states 'The only data available, apart from Laycock's fieldnotes, are a short word list of Gapun published by Höltker (1938)'.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik Languages: Checklist and Preliminary Classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. (entry 123 Bungain, pp. 35-36; Gapun sub-phylum notes)
sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives villages, informants (test DCL70), the Terebu/Kaiep name confusion, and a typological remark (subject prefixes, apparent gender concord); no phonology at all.

sources.citation: Gehberger, Johann, S.V.D. 1950. Aus dem Mythenschatz der Samap an der Nordostküste Neuguineas. Anthropos 45(1-3): 295ff. (Zur Einführung, pp. 295-296: language groupings of the Turubu mission area).
sources.note: No phonology content: an ethnographic myth collection whose introduction only enumerates the languages of the mission district (Melanesian Kaiep/Turubu/Samap; Papuan Bungain, Komassau, Tumaru; Forok as 'Mischsprache'; Mandi). Myths are given in German only.
